raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Python's `PrometheusStatLogger` creates every per-engine request series when the frontend starts, including one `vllm:request_success` child per `FinishReason`, so a fresh server exports them with value 0. The Rust frontend creates each series on first use, so a series appears only when a request first records into it. This PR creates them at startup. ## Claims - Right after startup, the Rust frontend exports zero-valued request series per engine: `vllm:request_success` for all five finish reasons, plus the request token counters and histograms. - `increase()`/`rate()` no longer lose the first increment of a series that previously appeared with value 1. For example, the shipped Grafana dashboard's `sum by(finished_reason) (increase(vllm:request_success_total[...]))` missed the first abort after startup. ## Validation Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root: ``` cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check # ok cargo sort --workspace --check rust # ok cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # ok cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings # ok cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast # 2311 tests run: 2311 passed, 13 skipped ``` - `connecting_exports_zero_valued_request_metrics_before_any_request` (`rust/src/llm/tests/generate.rs`) connects to a mock engine, sends no request, and snapshots the zero-valued series; it fails on `main`, where no series is rendered. - The existing request-metrics tests (`generate_records_request_metrics_in_prometheus_output`, `generate_without_engine_stats_exports_only_frontend_observed_metrics`, `dropping_stream_records_abort_terminal_request_metrics`, the server's `metric_delta` checks) pass unchanged. ## Details Python: `create_metric_per_engine(...)` in `PrometheusStatLogger.__init__` (`vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py`), and `for reason in FinishReason:` for `vllm:request_success` (`loggers.py:807-819`). Rust before: `RequestMetricsTracker::new` (`rust/src/llm/src/request_metrics.rs`) resolved the handles with `get_or_create` on every request, and `record_request_success` created a `finished_reason` child only on first use. Another consumer that saw the difference is `label_values(vllm:request_success_total, model_name)`, which stayed empty until the first request finished. Change: `Llm::new` resolves the request metric handles once per connected engine (the engine set is fixed at connect), and each request's tracker shares them through an `Arc`. `vllm:request_success` gets one counter per finish reason, chosen by an exhaustive `match` on `FinishReason`, so a new reason cannot go unexported. The per-request `get_or_create` lookups go away. The labels (served model name, engine index) and the engine-stats gate are fixed when `Llm` is built, so the handles are construction-time state of `Llm`; this mirrors how the engine-core client already pre-creates its scheduler and iteration series per engine in `ClientInner::new`. `EngineCoreClient::engine_indices` now derives each index the way `call` stamps it on the request stream (`engine_index().unwrap_or(0)`) instead of panicking on an identity that encodes no index, so the handle map is keyed exactly like the streams that look it up. Production identities always encode an index; only test engines do not. Known difference, unchanged: Python registers `vllm:corrupted_requests` only with `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS`; Rust always registers it, and now exports it from startup. Not a duplicate: no open PR pre-creates the Rust request series. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01K2SEJPm2Mawmm6pu8m9E1o ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

files.patch:
@@ -473,11 +473,13 @@ impl EngineCoreClient {
         self.inner.pending_utility_call_count()
     }
 
-    /// Return the engine-side indices connected to this client.
+    /// Return the engine-side indices connected to this client, as stamped on
+    /// request output streams: an engine identity that does not encode an
+    /// index maps to 0, as in [`Self::call`].
     pub fn engine_indices(&self) -> Vec<u32> {
         self.engines
             .iter()
-            .map(|engine| engine.engine_id.engine_index().expect("engine id must encode as u16"))
+            .map(|engine| engine.engine_id.engine_index().unwrap_or(0))
             .collect()
     }
